fixed_case_observations.depth_error: R improves global AbsRel most. L reduces whiteboard error but has larger wall errors than R. Both retain chair-rim errors.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: Most whiteboard edges remain red (missed) for all methods. LoRA F1 .336 is below R .367 and B0 .369; no broad boundary recovery.

fixed_case_observations.depth_error: L has less regression than R but both are worse than B0 globally. L lowers coffee-table surface/background error versus R.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: Table side edges match, but thin table legs and large sofa contours are still missed. L F1 .543 lies between B0 .537 and R .558.

fixed_case_observations.depth_error: Both adaptations are worse than B0. L shows less wall-texture error than R but persistent chair/counter errors.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: Most counter rim is missed and central chair has unmatched/missed segments for all methods. L F1 .506 is slightly below B0/R .515.

fixed_case_observations.depth_error: Large LoRA global improvement: B0/R/L AbsRel .5841/.4031/.2217. Background and furniture error falls, while foreground/branch errors remain substantial.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: Person/column contours match in all methods, but thin branches remain displaced or missed; L F1 .499 is below R .510 and B0 .509. Major global gain is not a boundary-recovery claim.

fixed_case_observations.depth_error: LoRA regresses versus both R and B0; wall/floor errors are brighter. AbsRel B0/R/L .1129/.0945/.1411.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: Foreground sofa contours are mostly matched but lamp/background contours remain red and upper hanging-object edge remains yellow. L F1 .490 is below R .514 and B0 .508.

fixed_case_observations.depth_error: Modest LoRA global gain with redistribution: shelf error reduces while left-curtain error increases.
fixed_case_observations.boundary: LoRA matches more of the right shelf vertical edges and some upper short edges; many pan/other shelf contours still missed. F1 B0/R/L .162/.215/.475. This is a genuine local edge benefit, not uniform recovery.

conclusions: Matched-seed LoRA improves AbsRel, RMSE and boundary-band AbsRel over R, but delta1 and macro boundary F1 decrease. The validation-best rule remains AbsRel.

Paired scene-bootstrap intervals cross zero for AbsRel/RMSE/delta1/F1; the boundary-band AbsRel interval is below zero. Intervals are descriptive conditional on this one training seed, not proof of a method winner.
The LoRA training-loss curve continues down while validation plateaus with excursions. This is a generalization/overfitting diagnostic, not a demonstrated causal explanation.
Best step2500 and stopping step3500 differ. No terminal 500-step suffix satisfies the frozen 1% stability criterion. The .10 target window starts600 and is confirmable only at800.
Two AMP overflow skips are recorded (12 and1064); training succeeds without changing batch or configuration. AMP skips are not failed training jobs.
R uses cached frozen features whereas L computes live foundation features. Report R cache-generation cost separately; do not treat training-only time as end-to-end speed.

Fixed cases were chosen before these results and preserve improvements and regressions. Boundary overlays use the same numerical definition and 2px tolerance; GT boundaries need not follow every RGB edge.
